sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Florida housing?
sections.html:
Florida's housing stock is large, mostly owner-occupied and carries a median owner value of $359,000 for 2020 to 2024. The Census Bureau counts 10,789,047 housing units on July 1, 2025, for a state of 23,462,518 people (Census Bureau QuickFacts, Florida).

The state grew 8.9 percent between the April 2020 estimates base and July 2025. Population per square mile was 401.4 in 2020, up from 350.6 in 2010, on 53,652.17 square miles of land. Those figures explain why Florida sellers often compete with a steady stream of new construction as well as resales: the bureau recorded 178,297 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How many Florida homes are owned and how many rented?
sections.html:
About two of every three. The owner-occupied housing unit rate is 67.6 percent for 2020 to 2024, which leaves roughly a third of occupied homes in the rental market. Households total 8,752,810, averaging 2.51 persons each.

Mobility is modest. Of persons aged one and older, 86.3 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. For a seller, that means most neighbors are staying put, and a listing draws from a pool of arrivals as much as from local move-up buyers.

Age matters too. The bureau puts residents 65 and over at 22.8 percent of the population, and veterans at 1,327,071. Both groups tie into the homestead benefits that the Department of Revenue describes for seniors and disabled veterans, which can shape what a buyer or heir pays after a sale.

sections.h2: What does it cost to own or rent in Florida?
sections.html:
Median selected monthly owner costs are $1,959 with a mortgage and $673 without one, while median gross rent is $1,669. All three are 2020 to 2024 figures from the American Community Survey as published in QuickFacts.

The gap between the two owner figures is a useful reminder. A paid-off house still carries taxes, insurance and upkeep, but the mortgage is the largest single piece. Sellers who inherited a free-and-clear house often find holding costs are low enough to feel no pressure, yet vacancy, repairs and the November tax bill continue.

The median household income is $74,568 in 2024 dollars and per capita income is $42,609. Persons in poverty are 12.0 percent of the population.

sections.h2: How do Florida's tax rules shape what a seller keeps?
sections.html:
Two items hit almost every sale. The first is documentary stamp tax on the deed. The Department of Revenue says the rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, where it is 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that does not apply to a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. All parties to the document are liable, whichever one agrees to pay (Department of Revenue, documentary stamp tax).

The second is the clerk's recording charge under s. 28.24(13): $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus a $1.00 first-page and $0.50 additional-page trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge (Florida Statutes, s. 28.24).

The property tax calendar matters as well. Assessment is as of January 1, bills go out in November, and the early-payment discount steps down from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February.

sections.h2: How does the homestead system affect buyers and sellers?
sections.html:
It creates a gap between what long-time owners pay and what newcomers pay. Save Our Homes caps assessed-value growth for a homestead at the lower of 3 percent or CPI, and a sale resets the property to just value the next January 1 (Department of Revenue assessment guide).

Non-homestead property is capped at a 10 percent yearly rise. That is one reason an investor-owned rental and a neighboring owner-occupied house can carry very different bills.

  • Check the property appraiser's record for the current assessed and just values.
  • Ask the tax collector whether any deferral or installment plan is attached.
  • Confirm that the exemption is still on the roll if the owner moved out.

None of this appears in a median value, so local records matter more than statewide averages.

sections.h2: What should a Florida seller verify before relying on market averages?
sections.html:
Look at the specific county, neighborhood and house, because a statewide median covers beach condos, inland ranch homes and rural parcels in one number. QuickFacts publishes the same set of rows for each county and city, so compare the place where the house sits.

The county property appraiser publishes assessed and just values, the clerk records deeds and collects doc stamp tax, and the tax collector sends bills. Those offices hold the facts that determine closing costs and the timeline, and each is elected under the county's structure.

Median sale price, days on market and sales volume are market-data items that QuickFacts does not carry. Ask a local agent or the clerk for recorded sales if you need them.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Florida?
faqs.a: $359,000 for owner-occupied housing units, using 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey data in Census QuickFacts. It reflects owners' estimates, so it is not a recorded sale price.

faqs.q: What share of Florida homes are owner-occupied?
faqs.a: 67.6 percent for 2020 to 2024. Households total 8,752,810, with 2.51 persons per household on average.

faqs.q: What is the median rent in Florida?
faqs.a: Median gross rent is $1,669 for 2020 to 2024. Median monthly owner costs are $1,959 with a mortgage and $673 without one.

faqs.q: How many housing units does Florida have?
faqs.a: 10,789,047 as of July 1, 2025, according to the Census Bureau's V2025 estimates. The state's population estimate for that date is 23,462,518.

faqs.q: Do Florida sellers pay a deed tax?
faqs.a: Yes, documentary stamp tax applies to deeds at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties. Miami-Dade uses 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cent surtax that is not due on a single-family dwelling transfer. All parties are liable to the state, whoever agrees to pay.
